steps_walked.title: Living sources tab, Storage budgets panel, per-lane transport lines in the "Go online?" popup, the retired scheduler mode, and the encrypted upgrade of a real install (brief S04-08)
prerequisites: THROWAWAY folder for O1-O11, in ONE terminal used only for throwaways. From the repository folder: (1) . .venv/bin/activate  (2) export OO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/oo-rowO-throwaway" OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 OO_AUTOSEED=0  (3) echo "$OO_DATA_DIR", which must print the throwaway path and never your real folder  (4) PYTHONPATH=. python docs/audit/living-sources-clickthrough-2026-09-25/seed.py  (5) PYTHONPATH=. python docs/audit/storage-budgets-clickthrough-2026-09-25/seed.py  (6) OO_PORT=8011 open-omniscience, then open http://127.0.0.1:8011. Run both seeds BEFORE starting the app, because they write to the database directly. Without OO_DATA_DIR, a run from the repository writes to the repository's own data/ folder, which may be your real one. OO_AUTOSEED=0 stops the app loading its catalogue of sources and legal documents at start; without it, the Law figures in O5 will not match. The first seed makes the Wikipedia stream's changes, a stored diff, an open gap, two tracked pages, two law documents and three map regions (downloaded, paused by airplane mode, failed). The second adds 19 days of corpus size history. scripts/ui_clickthrough_seed.py is NOT needed.
On the throwaway a language/terms page may appear: pick English and accept. The first-run guide may then open: close it with the × at its top right. NEVER press its 'Go online & start collecting'.
The app always starts in airplane mode (the plane icon in the top bar is filled). Only O11 (optional, throwaway) and possibly O13 (your real install, your normal collection) go online.
For O12: a second, empty throwaway folder. The commands are in O12.

Your REAL encrypted install and its passphrase, used only in O13-O15. Before upgrading it, keep the safety copy you normally make before any upgrade. Run O13-O15 in a NEW terminal where OO_DATA_DIR, OO_DB_PLAINTEXT and OO_AUTOSEED are NOT set.
A browser window you can narrow to phone width (about 375 px), or the browser's device mode, for O10.

Q1128 = a asks for the pass to be recorded per surface. Keep one short note each for: Storage panel, Living sources, the popup's transport lines, the task-manager cause lines, the scheduler panel, and the encrypted upgrade. For each, write the date, the languages seen, pass or fail, and anything odd. Times in the app are UTC, so in Paris summer time they read two hours behind your clock. That is by design.

steps.where: Sidebar (bottom) → Settings → subtab "Data & backup" in the strip under the top bar (#set-data) → the "Storage" panel at the top (#storage-panel) — throwaway, English
steps.do: Read the panel top to bottom. Hover these: the line starting "This machine, read at boot", the lane name "Wikipedia / Wikimedia", the Corpus growth figure, the Wikipedia row's "Not measured yet", one "No published budget", one "Not built yet", and the caveat line at the bottom of the panel.
steps.expect: Storage is a PANEL at the top of Data & backup, not a new subtab. The subtabs are still nine: Graphics · General · Cards · AI · Wikipedia · OpenStreetMap · Agenda · Data & backup · Advanced. Line 1 reads "This machine, read at boot: N CPU cores · X GB of RAM · Y GB of free disk" with your machine's numbers; its hover says it was read with no network. Line 2 reads "The published budgets are sized for a reference machine with 2 CPU cores and 3.5 GB of RAM. Raise them if this machine has more room." There is NO verdict between the two lines: no "too small" or "enough", and no red or green. The table header reads Lane · On disk · Budget · Growth, last 30 days, and there are four rows. (1) Corpus: a small size (about 1 MB), "No published budget", "+6.0 MB in 19 days" with "≈ +9.5 MB per 30 days at that rate" under it. (2) Wikipedia / Wikimedia: a size in KB (about 150 KB), "20 GB the published default", "<1% used" (never "0% used"), a number box with "Save budget", and growth "Not measured yet". (3) Law and (4) Maps / OpenStreetMap: "Not built yet", "No published budget", and an empty growth cell. Under the table, in grey: "Disk left: … free of … on the drive that holds your data folder." and "Your budgets can still take …; the drive has … free." That second line turns to the caveat colour only if your drive has under about 20 GB free, which is also correct. This caveat is visible without hovering: "Growth is each lane's own size change over the last 30 days, shown once there are 7 days of readings. It is a rate, not a forecast." Hovers: Wikipedia / Wikimedia says its file is encrypted with the same passphrase when your corpus is. The Corpus growth says "Measured from 3 readings of this lane's own size, <date> to <date>. A rate, not a forecast." "Not measured yet" says "A rate needs 7 days of this lane's size readings; there are 2 so far." "No published budget" says "No budget has been decided for this lane, so none is shown. The app never invents one." "Not built yet" says "This lane arrives in a later release. It has no file yet." The caveat's hover gives the method: -wal and -shm sidecars, at most hourly, whole MiB, 1 GB = 1024³ bytes. Nothing anywhere forecasts when the disk will be full.

(4) Walk Rome · eng · create · +16 · "Text stored; there was no earlier stored text to compare it with." Hovers: "Last change recorded" says it covers every page, followed or not, which is why it is later than the newest row. "Complete through" explains it is the earliest point every feed was read without a break. +38 says "Change in size, in bytes, as the source reported it." "log" says "The source's own word for this change, shown as it was sent." The tab shows no "undefined", "null" or "NaN", and no score or verdict.

WHAT CLOSES THE ROW: all six build slices (S1-S6) are built. Row O stays PARTIAL only on the brief's §5 operator steps. Step 1 is the upgrade of the maintainer's encrypted install (O13, O15). Step 2 is the maintainer's own click-through of the two new surfaces and the popup's transport lines, recorded per surface (O1-O12, O14). Step 3, the Q1016 NOTE, is already answered «Main tab» (R32). O11 is optional, because the sandbox walk covered it. O12 is recommended: it is the only place a human sees the absent-lane wording and the retired-mode notice.

ORDER MATTERS. Run the throwaway steps O1-O11 in order, with the optional online step LAST. Going online starts the scheduler, and its idle maintenance may record a fresh hourly size reading that replaces the seeded growth figures. Use one terminal only for throwaways, and a fresh one without OO_DATA_DIR, OO_DB_PLAINTEXT or OO_AUTOSEED for your real install.

DISCREPANCIES FOUND WHILE CHECKING THE CODE, for whoever records the result:
(1) The gate's S3 text says both new collection opt-ins "default OFF". The statistics refresh has defaulted ON since ruling R31 (2026-09-25; src/scheduler/settings.py:116-127), and its own hover says "On by default". The gate text is stale. An install that saved the schedule between PR #1178 and R31 honestly keeps its stored OFF.
(2) The gate and brief speak of corpus.db + wiki.db + law.db + osm.db. On main only wiki.db can ever be created, and the main file is open_omniscience.db.
(3) The reader's "tracked changes on this machine" link appears only for a Wikipedia article that carries a stored revision number AND whose page is tracked. The seeded folder has no such article, so O4 uses the ?wikitc= address directly.
(4) The gate says the lane file is "created at first enablement". On an upgraded install, wiki.db appears only once the stream first stores something online, or when a watched page is added. Until then Storage honestly says "Not created yet".
(5) The sandbox walks all ran with OO_AUTOSEED=0. Without it the app loads its source and legal-document catalogue at start, and the Law figures in O5 no longer read 2 / 2 / 1.
(6) LIKELY FINDING to record: the Living sources backup row's reason ("a lane is a live encrypted database; its backup format is not settled yet") has no key in any of the 12 locale files. It stays English in fr, ar and zh, although it is a caveat, and caveats ship in 12 languages.
(7) Minor, only if you open Export / Backup on the empty throwaway or before wiki.db exists: the Living sources row reads "(0 · 0 B)", while Storage says "Not created yet" for the same absent file.

THINGS THE SANDBOX WALKS SAW THAT ARE NOT ROW-O FAILURES: the line the scheduler's "Preview targets" button prints stays English in fr and ar. The OSM region name "Antarctica" has no key in any locale. Flag codes such as large-removal are shown as stored. After switching to French, the Home strip's "Your library is empty…" and "Automatic collection: stopped" stayed English. /api/briefing answered 500 on those builds and was handled in PR #1181; if Home shows "The briefing could not be read just now", that belongs to another thread.

SAFETY: O11 goes online only in the throwaway, pointed at a dead local SOCKS port with remote name resolution. With the Wi-Fi off it cannot reach anything at all. O13 may go online on your real install, which is simply your normal collection. Delete ~/oo-rowO-throwaway, ~/oo-rowO-mode and the O15 copy when done; the O15 copy is your whole corpus.

walk.summary: On this walk the click-through clause closes for every surface a throwaway can show. Storage, Living sources (all three subtabs, the diff, tracked changes and the deep link), the per-lane Transport lines in both fetch modes, the task-manager cause lines, the export member row and the retired-scheduler-mode notice all matched the gate. That held in en, fr and ar, in a zh spot check and at 375 px, on an ENCRYPTED seeded store, with 0 page errors and nothing going online. The row does not close yet because O13-O15 need the maintainer's real encrypted install and O11's online half could not be clicked here. Their encrypted-throwaway analogs all pass: the lane is encrypted with the same passphrase, law and osm are absent, and an app-stopped folder copy unlocks and matches. Four findings, none blocking: the backup-row reason is untranslated (P2), the offline coach covers row-O controls until dismissed (P3), the export row shows '(0 · 0 B)' for an absent lane (P3), and the task-manager tab title is untranslated (P3).

verdicts.title: The Living sources backup-row reason is untranslated: it stays English in fr, ar and zh
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on a fresh encrypted instance (8836, the row-O seeds run with OO_DB_PASSPHRASE; booted locked; unlocked through #pw/#btn-unlock). Settings > Data & backup > Export / Back up… was opened in en, fr, ar and zh through the top-bar switcher. The row label is translated ('Sources vivantes (1 · 480.0 KB)', 'المصادر الحيّة', '活跃信息源'). The #oo-tip text on hover is 'a lane is a live encrypted database; its backup format is not settled yet' in all four languages. OOI18N.t() on that exact string returns English (a pure dictionary lookup), and no src/static/locales/*.json file has the key. Re-graded P2 -> P3. The row is correctly disabled and unticked, and its visible label is translated; only the explanation's language is wrong. It does break the 'every caveat string ×12' rule, so it should still be fixed before the tag. It is also mostly moot for now: the bubble that carries it is drawn behind the modal dialog in every language (see the NEW finding below). Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/O-recheck/raw-i18n.json (living_row_tip and diag_t_reason per language) and Orc-export-fr.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/backup/inventory.py:118 sends the English sentence as not_exportable_reason. src/static/app-backup.js:265 renders it through t(d.not_exportable_reason), but the key is missing from all 12 locale files. The i18n gate (scripts/i18n_report.py) only collects literal strings from the static files and main.py's reader, so a server-sent string routed through t() is invisible to its 100% check.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add the key 'a lane is a live encrypted database; its backup format is not settled yet' to src/static/locales/en.json (identity) and translate it in the other 11 files. Optionally have tests/test_backup_inventory.py assert that every not_exportable_reason is a key in en.json, so the next server-sent reason cannot slip past the gate.

verdicts.title: The offline coach (#net-coach) covers row-O controls until 'Not now' is pressed. In Arabic it lands on the top-bar cluster itself
verdicts.reason: Reproduced with real Playwright clicks. The coach was shown on the second launch of a fresh profile, as a real user sees it. (1) At 1440x950 in fr, the coach at [1162..1432 x 62..235] hides the whole 'Avancé' subtab; a click on it times out with the coach intercepting. In en it only clips the Advanced tab's edge (x 1162..1178), so clicks work. (2) At 375x800 in en, all three Living sources subtabs (Wikipedia, Law, Maps) sit under the coach, and the Law click is intercepted. (3) NEW and worse: when the coach is first shown with the UI already in Arabic (1440 and 1024 wide), it is placed to the right of the plane at [232..502 x 8..143]. There it covers the top-bar W toggle (#wiki-toggle), the speed knob (#rate-toggle) and the task-manager icon (#tm-open). Trial clicks on all three are intercepted, a real click on #tm-open opens nothing, and all become clickable after 'Not now'. The plane, the language switcher and the shutdown button stay reachable. This matches the walker's 'in another run the Tasks & system icon'. It is the same class as the recorded P0 'net-coach-blocks-topbar-buttons' and the row-O S5 fix 'the offline hint covered the open language menu', so the project treats a coach covering controls as a defect; no ruling asks for it. (4) A coach placed in en is not moved when the UI flips to RTL: it stays at the right edge while the plane moves to x 186..220. Re-graded P3 -> P2 because of the RTL top-bar case. Frequency caveat: the walker's harness used a fresh browser profile on every run, so it met the coach every time. A real operator sees it on at most 6 launches (prominent on 2), and one 'Not now' retires it for good. Evidence: raw-coach-narrow.json, raw-rtl-coach.json, raw-rtl-trial.json, Orc-coach-settings-fr.png, Orc-coach-living-375-en.png, Orc-coach-covers-topbar-1440-ar.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-core.js:1025-1026: the 'prefer to the right of the button' branch checks only that the viewport has room. It never checks the protected cluster, and in RTL the #wiki-toggle, #rate-toggle and #tm-open buttons sit to the plane's right. app-core.js:1034-1037: the 'below' branch guards only the top-bar buttons, so the coach drops onto the active tab's subtab strip (app.css:1803: position:fixed, z-index 360). app-core.js:1087: re-placement listens only to 'resize', never to 'oo:langchange' or a direction flip.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In _placeCoach, build the guard rects first: net-toggle, lang-switch, tm-open, app-shutdown, rate-toggle and wiki-toggle, plus the visible subtab strip of the active tab ('nav.tabs' with a non-zero rect). Accept the side placement only if the candidate rect intersects none of them; otherwise place the coach below the lowest guard (top = max bottom + gap). Also call _placeCoach on 'oo:langchange', next to the existing resize listener.

verdicts.title: The Export / Backup dialog shows 'Living sources (0 · 0 B)' for an absent lane while Storage says 'Not created yet'
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on an empty encrypted instance (8837, no wiki.db). Storage reads 'Wikipedia / Wikimedia · Not created yet', and the Export dialog reads 'Living sources (0 · 0 B)'. The two cells state different facts, though. Storage gives one lane's on-disk size, where absent and 0 B differ. The export row gives a member's count of stores and the bytes an export of it would write. With no lane file both really are 0, and every other empty member in the same dialog reads the same way: 'LLM models (0 · 0 B)', 'Offline maps (0 · 0 B)', 'Wikipedia dumps (0 · 0 B)'. The 'absent is not zero' comment in inventory.py is about the per-lane breakdown, and there the absent lane is correctly left out ('breakdown': {}). The member totals are pinned on purpose. tests/test_backup_inventory.py::test_an_ABSENT_lane_is_left_out_rather_than_reported_as_zero_bytes asserts breakdown == {}, count == 0 and bytes == 0 for an absent lane, with the docstring 'A lane the operator has never opened must not appear in a backup dialog as an empty one'. Q219 = a asks for 'their sizes shown before the export starts', meaning the size the export would write, which is 0 B. The walker misapplied a breakdown-level comment to the member total. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/O-recheck/raw-absent.json and Orc-export-absent-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: Not a defect. src/backup/inventory.py:103-121 leaves absent lanes out of the breakdown and totals the member as 0 stores / 0 bytes. src/static/app-backup.js:268 prints the same '(count · bytes)' format for every member.
verdicts.suggested_fix: None required. If the maintainer wants the export row to echo Storage's wording, render '(none yet)' when d.count === 0 for every member in opt(), not only for lanes, so the dialog keeps one convention.

verdicts.title: The task-manager tab title stays 'Task manager · FOOS' in fr, ar and zh
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: the #tm-open real click opens /tasks, and after 2 s and again after 7 s document.title is 'Task manager · FOOS' in en, fr, ar and zh. On the same page the h1 is translated ('Gestionnaire de tâches', 'مدير المهام', '任务管理器'), the tabs are translated, and ar has dir=rtl. The key exists: fr.json:4049 has 'Task manager · FOOS': 'Gestionnaire de tâches · FOOS', and ar and zh carry it too. OOI18N.t('Task manager · FOOS') on that page returns the translation. So the string is keyed but never applied. The walker's attribution is not quite right: the page is not simply 'never re-set'. The i18n pass that could translate the title runs before the locale has loaded. Cosmetic, P3 as reported. Evidence: raw-i18n.json (tm_title_2s, tm_title_7s, diag_t_title_key per language) and Orc-tm-fr.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/taskmanager.html:200-205: applyLang() calls OOI18N.setLang(lang) without awaiting it (setLang is async and fetches the locale), then immediately calls OOI18N.apply(document) while the map is still empty. That pass records the English <title> text as the original and leaves it English. setLang's own later apply() and the MutationObserver both use document.body (src/static/i18n.js:85 'root = root || document.body', and the observer on document.body), so the <head><title> text node is never walked again.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In taskmanager.html applyLang(): Promise.resolve(lang && OOI18N.setLang(lang)).then(() => OOI18N.apply(document)). Add document.addEventListener('oo:langchange', () => OOI18N.apply(document.head)) so the page's own language menu (pickLang) also retitles the tab. The first-seen English cache means re-applying is safe.

verdicts.title: NEW, found during the recheck: every #oo-tip hover inside a modal dialog is drawn BEHIND the dialog, so no user can read the consent popup's per-lane hosts/transport or the export row's reason
verdicts.reason: While hovering the Export dialog's Living sources row, #oo-tip has class 'show', opacity 1 and the right text. But its rect [732..1062 x 371..425] is painted under the modal: only the fragment 'ackup' peeks out past the dialog's right edge, dimmed by the backdrop (Orc-export-hover-living-en.png, Orc-export-hover-living-crop-en.png). In the Go online? popup (#net-consent, :modal = true), hovering 'Press collection' puts the bubble at [579..909 x 313..385], entirely inside the dialog's footprint, and nothing is visible (Orc-consent-hover-en.png). The sandbox record docs/audit/lane-transport-clickthrough-2026-09-25/consent-protected-en.png shows no bubble either. The walker's O7/O8/O9 hover evidence, like the earlier audits', was read from #oo-tip's textContent, not seen. show() also removes the title attribute, so no native tooltip appears as a fallback, and keyboard focus uses the same bubble. For a human, row O's 'Each lane declares its transport in the consent hover' (and row H's per-lane host list) cannot be read. The consent gate itself is intact: the popup still gates, Stay offline kept {online:false}, and nothing went online. That makes this P1, a failure of the informed-consent disclosure layer (non-negotiable + invariants #14/#17), rather than a P0 consent bypass. Nothing in the ledger records it. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/O-recheck/raw-tip-modal.json.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:259-267 creates #oo-tip and appends it to document.body. Dialogs opened with showModal() (e.g. #ux-export at src/static/app-backup.js:46, and #net-consent) are in the browser's top layer, which paints above any z-index, so app.css:1793's z-index:400 cannot lift the bubble over them. app-boot.js:281 removes the element's title during show(), which suppresses the native tooltip as well.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In show() (app-boot.js:277), move the bubble into the top layer when the target is inside an open modal. Either make it a manual popover (tip.popover = 'manual' once, then tip.showPopover() in show() and tip.hidePopover() in hide(); a popover opened after the modal stacks above it), or append it to the nearest open dialog: const host = el.closest('dialog[open]') || document.body; if (tip.parentNode !== host) host.appendChild(tip); (position:fixed still resolves to the viewport). Add a Chromium test that hovers a #net-consent lane and asserts the bubble's centre pixel is not covered by the dialog.
